author: ToolSpeed Exploratory Research Group
purpose: Exploratory evaluation protocol testing whether a fast TypeSafe/Jev System One probabilistic router can improve ToolSpeeder's speculative read execution after fully accounting for provider latency, wasted calls, failure modes, and safety invariants.
status_note: EXPLORATORY PROTOCOL ONLY. This protocol is distinct from the frozen confirmatory protocol tool-speed-v1.3.json. Findings from this protocol cannot be represented as confirmatory evidence.

pre_registered_hypotheses.H1_latency: Jev produces a statistically supported improvement in Correct Completion Latency (CCL) in workload regions where downstream tool latency exceeds the break-even threshold.
pre_registered_hypotheses.H2_correctness: Task success/correctness under Jev is non-inferior to existing E3 and no-speculation baselines.
pre_registered_hypotheses.H3_prediction_quality: Jev reported probabilities correlate with actual speculation correctness, yielding Brier score better than random uniform guessing (< 0.25).
pre_registered_hypotheses.H4_safety: Zero unauthorized or mutative speculative executions across all trials (kill condition if violated).
pre_registered_hypotheses.H5_net_utility: Jev overhead must not consume more time than it saves except in sub-break-even tool latency regions.
pre_registered_hypotheses.H6_graceful_degradation: Provider failure (timeout, 429, 401, network disconnect) falls back without causing task execution failure.

kill_conditions: Any unauthorized mutative or approval-requiring speculative execution occurs.
Oracle or expected-output leakage enters provider state or execution history.
TypeSafe output creates or mutates tool arguments instead of selecting predefined candidates.
Live API credentials or secrets enter logs, traces, or evidence bundles.
Live provider results are labeled or represented as deterministic replay evidence, or vice versa.
Failed tasks are omitted from latency accounting.
TypeSafe provider inference latency is excluded from end-to-end timing.
Thresholds are retrospectively tuned and presented as confirmatory.
